# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve issue that requires medication and regular monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties and is a picky eater, which may affect her growth and overall health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which means her muscles are too stiff sometimes, and requires therapy and exercise to manage it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear last month and has had issues with hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision and may need to have her eyes checked.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has frequent dental issues, including cavities, and needs regular check-ups and fillings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing issues may affect her schoolwork.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often need extra help in school and may require special education plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder and ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia and scoliosis, which affect her walking and running and require regular monitoring and physical therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and spinal issues.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups and monitoring for the patient's dental issues
* Regular hearing reviews and monitoring for the patient's hearing issues
* Eye exams to monitor the patient's vision and address any concerns
* Cardiac monitoring and medication management for the patient's heart valve issue
* Physical therapy and exercise to manage the patient's hypotonia
* Monitoring and management of the patient's hip dysplasia and scoliosis
* Consideration of referral for endocrine investigations if the patient's growth velocity is a concern
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart condition that requires specialist review.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is a slow gainer when it comes to weight and eats well but doesn't seem to put on weight as quickly as her peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets really tired when playing or running around, and it's not just being lazy; she genuinely can't keep up like other kids.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing and often asks for things to be repeated, and she has had trouble with her ears.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things clearly, often squints, and her eyes get tired easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had trouble with her teeth and requires regular dental check-ups and treatments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome can have weak enamel, and regular dental check-ups are important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes a bit longer to learn new things and reach milestones than expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech came in later than it did for her siblings, and she takes a bit longer to learn new things and reach milestones than expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, and some may have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups and treatments for the patient's teeth
* Regular hearing reviews for the patient
* Eyesight review for the patient
* Cardiac review for the patient
* Consideration of a palate review for the patient
* Referral for a skeletal review for the patient
* Monitoring of the patient's growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if necessary
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy for the patient as needed

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily when playing with friends or running around and can't seem to keep up with physical activity for as long as other kids his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's weight gain has been slower compared to his peers, and his parents have had to work harder to ensure he's eating enough and getting the nutrients he needs.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting, and has a speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat themselves because he didn't catch what they said the first time around, and has had issues with his ears that have required medical attention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains that things look blurry sometimes, and it's been an issue for a while now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to go to the dentist quite frequently, and they've found a few issues that need regular check-ins to prevent anything more serious from developing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a speech delay and seems behind other children in his development, and is working with therapists and doctors to try and help him catch up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a speech delay and seems behind other children in his development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing and address any concerns
* Eyesight review to monitor vision and address any concerns
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor skeletal development
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address any concerns.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quicker than other kids his age and needs to rest more often, suggesting possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has bowel problems, which are managed with diet and medication under the guidance of the healthcare team.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes has spells where he stares off into space, lasting for a few seconds before snapping back to attention, and has been observed to have developmental delays and learning difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with the condition.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets easily frustrated when there's too much noise around him, suggesting possible hearing or sensory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means he has trouble seeing things that are far away, and squints when trying to watch TV or look at things across the room.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs regular dental check-ups due to prone teeth and cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and learning difficulties, and his movements can appear a bit different from those of his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with the condition.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with hip dysplasia and has had treatment for it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's prone teeth and cavities.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight review to monitor the patient's vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review to investigate the patient's heart condition and provide appropriate management.
* Referral for a skeletal review to monitor the patient's spinal bones and address any concerns.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's developmental delays and learning difficulties.
* Monitoring of the patient's growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Management of the patient's bowel problems through diet and medication under the guidance of the healthcare team.
